Latest Update: Introducing in-place migration to GKE Dataplane V2

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • GKE Dataplane V2 is Google Cloud’s next-generation networking dataplane for Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), built on extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) and open-source Cilium to replace traditional iptables routing and kube-proxy.
  • Sources indicate that GKE customers consistently tell us that while they want to adopt GKE Dataplane V2 for its performance and scale, migrating production clusters carrying stateful workloads and established IP allocations has been challenging, often requiring a disruptive parallel cluster setup.
  • Let’s take a look at what GKE Dataplane V2 brings to the table and how to start migrating your environment to it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The front door to AI in the workplace.

GKE Dataplane V2 is Google Cloud’s next-generation networking dataplane for Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE), built on extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) and open-source Cilium to replace traditional iptables routing and kube-proxy. We built GKE Dataplane V2 to meet the performance, scalability, and security demands of modern cloud-native workloads.

Sources indicate that GKE customers consistently tell us that while they want to adopt GKE Dataplane V2 for its performance and scale, migrating production clusters carrying stateful workloads and established IP allocations has been challenging, often requiring a disruptive parallel cluster setup. Today, we are pleased to introduce the preview of in-place migration, allowing you to transition eligible VPC-native clusters from GKE Dataplane V1 to GKE Dataplane V2 directly.

Let’s take a look at what GKE Dataplane V2 brings to the table and how to start migrating your environment to it.

According to recent reports, GKE Dataplane V2 is built on the extended Berkeley Packet Filter (eBPF) and open-source Cilium, with features specifically tuned for performance, scalability, and deep integration with Google Cloud networking. Consider the following capabilities:.

Scale and performance: By handling packet processing with eBPF maps in the Linux kernel instead of linear iptables rules, GKE Dataplane V2 supports clusters of up to 15,000 nodes with network policy enforcement (and up to 65,000 nodes when network policy enforcement is disabled, which requires recreating clusters). This architecture also handles the high Pod churn, fast sandbox provisioning, and network identity scaling required by large agentic AI workloads.

High-throughput accelerator networking: Serves as the foundational networking layer for GPU and Cloud TPU clusters on GKE, helping keep accelerators computing rather than waiting on network initialization. It also powers capabilities like GKE managed DRANET for Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) of network devices.

Network security and observability: With GKE Dataplane V2, standard Kubernetes NetworkPolicy enforcement and hierarchical ClusterNetworkPolicy work directly in the kernel with optimized performance. GKE Dataplane V2 also provides the underlying dataplane for sidecarless GKE ambient networking, while GKE Dataplane V2 observability delivers native network policy logging, live traffic topology, and Hubble flow metrics.

Instead of having to manually move workloads to a new cluster, GKE now automates the transition across three stages, as described in the GKE Dataplane V2 migration guide:.

Sources indicate that 1. Eligibility and preflight checks: Before starting, verify that your Pod IP ranges have enough capacity to recreate the nodes by using GKE IP address utilization insights, and check Active Assist for incompatible configurations like custom eBPF programs on managed interfaces.

In a recent development, 2. Initiate the migration: Once you’ve verified the preflight checks, start the migration with a single Google Cloud CLI update command.

To initiate the migration on an eligible cluster, run:.

3. Automated rollout and finalization: GKE updates your node pools to GKE Dataplane V2 while respecting your configured maintenance windows, exclusions, and upgrade strategies. To move faster, you can also patch specific node pools manually, or roll back to GKE Dataplane V1 at any time prior to finalization.

According to recent reports, in-place migration supports VPC-native clusters running GKE 1.35 or later (see the migration guide for exact version requirements). It does not support routes-based clusters or clusters running Calico.

In-place migration to GKE Dataplane V2 is available now in preview. During this time, we recommend testing migrations on non-production or test clusters first as you strategy your broader transition.

To learn more about GKE Dataplane V2 and to get started:.

Review cluster eligibility and migration phases in About migrating to GKE Dataplane V2.

Follow the instructions in Migrate VPC-native clusters to GKE Dataplane V2.

Read GKE Network Interface, from kubenet to eBPF/Cilium to DRANET for background on the evolution of GKE CNIs.

Explore GKE networking dataplane for large agentic AI workloads to see how Dataplane V2 scales for large AI clusters.

Latest Update: Depth Before Breadth: Reverse-to-Forward Curriculum with Advantage Decomposition for LLM Agent

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (179 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

Recent findings suggest that arXiv:2611.24697v1 Announce Type: upcoming Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a common approach for training large language model (LLM) agents on long-horizon tasks. However, learning from sparse terminal rewards makes credit assignment and exploration difficult. We approach these challenges through a policy-induced capability region, the set of states from which the current policy can reliably complete a task. Near its boundary, an agent may need only a few actions to reach a more solvable state, even when the goal remains distant. This reduces long-horizon learning to two coupled subproblems of reaching that state and completing the task from there. We address them with paired advantages and a progressive reverse-to-forward curriculum. The advantages provide separate signals for reaching more solvable states and completing the task from them, while the curriculum expands the capability region backward along successful reference trajectories and then into off-reference states through on-policy exploration. On ALFWorld and WebShop, our method outperforms competitive agentic RL methods at both model scales, achieving success rates of 90.1%/96.1% and 80.2%/82.6% with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, respectively.

Movie2Game-Bench: Holistic Evaluation of Film-to-Game Adaptation Beyond Playability

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (172 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2611.24669v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adapting a film into a game requires selecting source elements and translating them into player actions, rules, and feedback. We introduce Movie2Game-Bench (M2G-bench), a benchmark for evaluating film-to-game adaptation beyond playability. M2G-bench combines general evaluation, movie-specific evaluation, and playtesting by three GUI model players. The protocol connects source content to gameplay steps and implementation evidence, capturing both content preservation and interactive realization. The benchmark comprises 22 films and 658 source-specific reference items. Evaluating 14 models on the same films with their selected primary harnesses reveals complementary strengths in game quality, adaptation, and player experience. A shared weakness concerns playable sequences: this category has the lowest content-presence mean in all 14 models, averaging 37.9 out of 100 compared with 54.8 for iconic elements. Among judgments of retained emotionaldevelopment content, narrative choices account for 60.0% and scenario operation for 7.2%. These findings identify two linked priorities for film-to-game adaptation: preserving source situations that can support gameplay and connecting retained content to player actions and consequences.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Starting today, Amazon RDS for MySQL supports MySQL major version 9.7, the latest Long-Term Support release from MySQL community.
  • The Replication Applier Metrics help you diagnose replication lag by adding two Performance Schema tables that report per-channel applier backlog, throughput, and wait statistics, along with each worker's progress on its current transaction.
  • You can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot.

Starting today, Amazon RDS for MySQL supports MySQL major version 9.7, the latest Long-Term Support release from MySQL community. Amazon RDS for MySQL 9.7 debuts with community MySQL 9.7.4. This launch introduces support for the Replication Applier Metrics component, JSON Duality Views, and Hypergraph Optimizer.

The Replication Applier Metrics help you diagnose replication lag by adding two Performance Schema tables that report per-channel applier backlog, throughput, and wait statistics, along with each worker's progress on its current transaction. JSON Duality Views let applications read and write the same relational tables as JSON documents. The Hypergraph Optimizer is an opt-in query optimizer that can improve execution intends for complex, multi-join queries. For more details, refer to the MySQL 9.7.4 release notes and the Amazon RDS for MySQL release notes.

You can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon RDS User Guide. This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for MySQL is available. Learn more about pricing details at Amazon RDS for MySQL pricing.

Sources indicate that amazon RDS for MySQL makes it simple to set up, operate, and scale MySQL deployments in the cloud. Create or enhancement a fully managed Amazon RDS database in the Amazon RDS Management Console or by using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).

Self-Rewarded Reinforcement Learning for Better-Structured Medical Explanations in Small Language Models

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (181 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

arXiv:2611.24650v2 Announce Type: new Abstract: Small language models (SLMs) can run on commodity hardware and support privacy-preserving, on-premises clinical deployment, but their medical explanations are often short and poorly structured compared with large language models. Recent supervised approaches such as Meerkat transfer chain-of-thought reasoning into 7B-8B backbones, yet their training objective does not directly target the style or organization of the generated rationales. Building on the instruction-tuned Mistral-7B backbone, we investigate whether a lightweight reinforcement learning (RL) step can improve explanation structure without human preference labels. We apply Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) with LoRA adaptation to 2000 Meerkat-derived medical prompts, guided by a simple self-supervised reward that favors longer, lexically diverse, and well-punctuated responses while penalizing very short ones. Training for about 170 PPO steps on a single NVIDIA A100 GPU yields a stable increase in the average reward. Quantitative and qualitative comparisons show that the RL-tuned model produces longer, more organized, multi-point explanations while preserving the underlying medical content. We discuss the promise and the limitations of self-rewarded RL for shaping the style of medical explanations.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Managing Director, Global Partner Marketing.

The front door to AI in the workplace.

At Google Cloud, our commitment to agentic transformation extends to everyone, including the partners who build and grow alongside us.

It has been revealed that today, we are excited to introduce new Gemini-powered co-marketing capabilities directly within everyday go-to-market workflows for our partners. These new features enable partners to produce customized, brand-aligned joint assets in minutes, scaling campaign execution and driving pipeline more effectively.

It has been revealed that as technology evolves and customer expectations shift, marketers are no longer just producing campaigns. We’re building continuous, hyper-personalized, data-driven demand engines, and we’re doing it across an increasingly fragmented buyer journey.

For our partner network, delivering on this expectation means solving a dual challenge: differentiating core offerings while articulating a unified vision with Google Cloud.

Bridging that gap at enterprise scale requires more than incremental efficiency — it requires agentic agility to jointly create, adapt, and distribute stories together that resonate.

The updated Partner Marketing Studio introduces a suite of agentic tools designed to accelerate campaign execution, optimize performance, and maximize impact for partners of all sizes.

Industry observers note that agentic search: Partners can now use a simple chat feature. Search for what you need, rather than navigating a content repository.

Brand alignment: Never worry about brand compliance again, with a brand reviewer agent that helps ensure your content upholds Google Cloud’s partner brand guidelines.

ISV asset creation: Gemini generated, high-fidelity marketing assets to drive demand to marketplace listings.

Social automation: A latest social editor with the ability to create posts across multiple networks simultaneously, add account tags, and refine messaging per channel with AI.

Customer case studies: An agent designed to build best-in-class customer success stories to highlight joint customer wins.

Gemini-Assisted Translation: Accelerate global marketing programs with agentic translations across 130 languages.

Natural language analytics: Gain end-to-end visibility connecting marketing execution directly to tangible business outcomes.

Sources indicate that "Partner Marketing Studio has become an extension of our partner marketing team. With built-in Gemini capabilities and ready-to-run joint campaigns, we can tailor high-impact marketing assets across industries, regions, and personas in minutes. It allows us to do more with less while accelerating pipeline for our joint solutions" - Liana Shuma, Global Head of Technology Partnerships, Pigment.

While the platform features powerful new tools, our core focus remains unchanged: helping you build your brand authority and generate pipeline demand.

Sources indicate that you will continue to find a curated content library structured specifically for you, highlighting top-performing campaigns aligned with Google Cloud strategic priority plays. Partners maintain full access to Google-produced localized campaign content and ready-made assets that can be customized to suit specific go-to-market objectives.

Furthermore, high-value partner services remain readily accessible within the platform:.

Applying to host customer events directly inside a Google office.

Requesting a Google Cloud speaker for your hosted events.

Attending dedicated office-hours sessions with Google Cloud marketing experts.

Requesting social amplification for campaigns.

According to recent reports, “Google offices are not only a great draw for attendees, but by handling all event logistics, Google Cloud saved us significant time, money, and allowed us to focus entirely on delivering high-impact content and driving audience engagement” - Jenny Bejarano. GTM Specialist, Tiger Analytics.

“We appreciate Google Cloud’s support with speakers for our events. This collaboration strengthens our credibility and value proposition with prospects” - Tommaso Vaccarella, Co-Founder & General Manager, Connected Stories.

Via Google Cloud Partner Network: Navigate to Resources > Marketing > Partner Marketing Studio.

Via direct browser link: Visit www.partnermarketingstudio.com directly.

In a recent development, these updates are part of Google Cloud’s larger commitment to transforming how we empower and enable partners with Gemini. In addition to Partner Marketing Studio, we’re leveraging Gemini throughout the partner experience, including a revamped partner marketing funds experience to streamline activity planning, simplify pipeline reporting, and proactively validate required documentation before submission.

Recent findings suggest that we’ve seen Google Cloud experience tremendous growth in recent years, and a major part of that success has been the incredible work done by our partner ecosystem. Now, as we’re bringing the power of Gemini directly into your go-to-market workflows, we’re excited to take our work together to a whole upcoming level.

With AI at our side, and as one of our strongest offerings, it will be easier than ever to create, connect, and grow together.

80% of mid-sized FS firms fear falling behind on AI

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (489 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Fintech

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mid-sized financial services firms are struggling to keep up with larger rivals on AI, with 80% of their leaders saying they are falling behind, according to research from TXP, a digital transformation business focused on tech consulting, development and resourcing.
  • The study points to a squeeze between thin in-house expertise and expensive outside partnerships.
  • It has been revealed that the report, titled ‘Partner Dependency: The Hidden Cost of AI Projects’, polled 200 executives shaping AI strategy at mid-market organisations, among them businesses in financial services and insurance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mid-sized financial services firms are struggling to keep up with larger rivals on AI, with 80% of their leaders saying they are falling behind, according to research from TXP, a digital transformation business focused on tech consulting, development and resourcing.

The study points to a squeeze between thin in-house expertise and expensive outside partnerships.

It has been revealed that the report, titled ‘Partner Dependency: The Hidden Cost of AI Projects’, polled 200 executives shaping AI strategy at mid-market organisations, among them businesses in financial services and insurance. Its central finding is that weak internal know-how, combined with poor handover of knowledge during projects, is locking firms into long-term reliance on external providers.

Some 65% of mid-market FS leaders said inadequate knowledge sharing has left them relying on outside partners to run or extend their AI initiatives. A further 56% admitted their staff cannot properly judge whether systems built by partners are working as intended.

Looking ahead, 77% expect this reliance to leave their own teams unable to oversee AI independently, and 79% fear it raises the likelihood that faults in AI systems will slip past unnoticed or prove impossible to resolve internally before they grow into larger problems.

Recent findings suggest that financial pressure is another concern. Of those surveyed, 91% believe dependence on partners could push expenses higher over time, while 56% mentioned spending on implementation partners has exceeded the value AI has delivered so far.

Trust in suppliers also emerged as an matter. Two-thirds of respondents claimed some partners had overstated their AI capabilities, with firms soon discovering a lack of genuine expertise. In such cases, organisations can face delayed projects or the added expense of hiring a second provider to finish the job.

TXP operates as a digital transformation specialist, offering tech consulting, development and resourcing services.

Industry observers note that TXP chief operations officer Tim Hurst mentioned, “Mid-sized financial services firms often have smaller budgets and fewer internal skills than large enterprises. To keep pace with complex, critical technologies such as AI, partnerships and external support are essential. But without effective knowledge transfer, partner support often becomes partner dependence once the initial delivery phase ends. Costs quickly rise as projects extend beyond implementation into ongoing management. The value of AI is eroded and errors become harder to spot and fix, introducing security and operational risk.”.

Hurst added, “AI shouldn’t be the sole domain of larger, well-funded FS firms, and partners play a key role in levelling the playing field by helping the mid-market realise the benefits of AI. Mid-sized businesses should look for partners with strong security and compliance credentials who can integrate AI with their existing systems. Knowledge transfer and a clear strategy to reduce long-term dependency should be built into every relationship from the start. Partners must build systems that work, and leave clients able to innovate long after they’ve gone.”.

Organisations across the region want firmer oversight of their sensitive data, technology and infrastructure, alongside greater resilience and less exposure to strategic dependencies on outside providers.

According to recent reports, saviynt provides AI-enabled, cloud-native identity security for organisations handling highly sensitive workloads. The new EU service adds to its existing data residency and private cloud options.

Because the offering runs independently of Saviynt’s global commercial cloud, customers can keep essential identity security functions running while cutting their reliance on external infrastructure and services.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Amazon Cognito now supports point-in-time recovery (PITR), so you can restore the user data in a user pool to an earlier time.
  • Industry observers note that with PITR, you choose a recovery point, preview how many consumers, groups, multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings, and passkeys the recovery will create, patch, or delete, and then start or cancel the recovery.
  • Sources indicate that PITR is enabled automatically for user pools on the Essentials and Plus feature aims at no additional charge.

Amazon Cognito now supports point-in-time recovery (PITR), so you can restore the user data in a user pool to an earlier time. Amazon Cognito helps you implement secure sign-in and access control for users, AI agents, and microservices. Previously, you had to build and maintain your own export and restore process, and restored users received new identifiers and had to reset their passwords.

Industry observers note that with PITR, you choose a recovery point, preview how many consumers, groups, multi-factor authentication (MFA) settings, and passkeys the recovery will create, patch, or delete, and then start or cancel the recovery. Recovered users keep their identifiers, passwords, MFA settings, and passkeys, so they can sign in without resetting their credentials. For example, if a script deletes or modifies users by mistake, you can restore the user data to the moment before it ran.

Sources indicate that PITR is enabled automatically for user pools on the Essentials and Plus feature aims at no additional charge. The recovery window is up to 1 day on Essentials and up to 14 days on Plus. You can initiate and manage a recovery using the AWS Management Console, the Amazon Cognito API, AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI), or AWS SDKs. PITR is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available. To learn more, see Point-in-time recovery in the Amazon Cognito Developer Guide.

The MoneyHelper Pensions Dashboard, a government-backed tool that will let savers view all their pensions in one place, will go live to the public in summer 2027, with pension schemes now under pressure to make sure the data behind it is accurate before launch.

Pensions minister Torsten Bell MP shared the timeline at a town hall event run by the Money and Pensions Service (MaPS) on 19 November 2026.

He told delegates that the first dashboard is now under a year away. He also confirmed that the Government still intends to give the industry six months’ warning of the exact public launch date.

The announcement follows the 31 October 2026 deadline for pension providers and schemes to join the dashboards ecosystem.

According to recent reports, more than 2,400 schemes and providers are now linked to the infrastructure, which covers upwards of 75 million records alongside millions of State Pension records. MaPS chief executive Oliver Morley used the event to thank the industry for meeting this connection target.

Sources indicate that consumer testing has reached its second phase. The number of consumers is being raised step by step so that the MoneyHelper dashboard can be refined as feedback comes in. Delegates at the town hall heard the newest findings from this testing.

MaPS also commissioned Ipsos to study how people use dashboards, and the research was presented at the event. People responded very positively. Some 75% said they were satisfied with the experience overall, and over 80% said they would return to the dashboard.

Once live, the service will give people a single view of their pension savings for the first time. The aim is to help them plan for retirement and manage their wider finances with better information.

The town hall gathered representatives from industry, government and regulators to review progress on the programme.

Government pensions minister Torsten Bell MP noted, “Pensions Dashboard are on track to transform how people understand their pensions. Being able to see your pensions in one place will give millions of savers something too many have missed out on for too long: a clear picture of their finances that helps them proposal ahead with confidence.

“Thanks to hard yards that have been put in across the industry, we can now look ahead to launch. Behind every pension is someone thinking about their future, and we want them to feel confident their pots are easy to find, secure and actually working to provide them with an income in retirement.”.

According to recent reports, money and Pensions Service CEO Oliver Morley added, “The milestones we have now reached with pensions dashboards are a testament to the dedication shown right across industry, government and regulators. Delivering dashboards is a partnership, and our town hall event celebrates what has been achieved.

“We are now building momentum towards the launch of the MoneyHelper Pensions Dashboard in Summer 2027. This is a once-in-a-generation opportunity to help people better understand and connect with their pensions.

“By continuing to work together, ensuring people can access high-quality pensions information and striving to deliver the best possible user experience, we will deliver a tool that helps people feel more informed and in control of their retirement planning.”.

The Pensions Regulator executive director for market oversight Ben Gunnee added, “Having millions of member records connected to pensions dashboards is a significant step towards members being able to find their pensions information in one place. But this is not the finish line.

“As we look ahead to launch, schemes should take the necessary steps to ensure the information members see is accurate, complete and up-to-date, and be ready to support those who engage with them, so members can reap the benefits of dashboards.”.

VisionX AI bets on graph AI to expose hidden crime networks

💡 Key Takeaways
  • VisionX AI, a Singapore-based AI-native RegTech firm operating as a standalone company within Alpha Ladder Group, has launched AEGIS, an in-house Large Graph Model (LGM) designed to detect and investigate financial crime, along with TraceX, the first product to run on it.
  • AEGIS takes a different approach from tools that assess payments one at a time.
  • In a recent development, visionX AI pairs this proprietary model with LLMs from established providers in a hybrid set-up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

VisionX AI, a Singapore-based AI-native RegTech firm operating as a standalone company within Alpha Ladder Group, has launched AEGIS, an in-house Large Graph Model (LGM) designed to detect and investigate financial crime, along with TraceX, the first product to run on it.

AEGIS takes a different approach from tools that assess payments one at a time. It uses a Graph Transformer architecture and was pretrained on graph data drawn from financial transactions, so it learns how wallets, accounts and entities link together and how money travels between them.

In a recent development, visionX AI pairs this proprietary model with LLMs from established providers in a hybrid set-up. AEGIS supplies the network intelligence, while the LLMs manage conversational interaction, reasoning and AI-supported investigative work. The combination aims to help banks and investigators surface concealed relationships, unusual fund movements and the wider criminal groups operating behind single transactions.

The launch comes as illicit finance grows more networked. In July 2026, the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) cautioned that criminal groups take advantage of the cross-border reach of virtual assets to defraud victims, dodge sanctions and launder money. Its findings revealed that illicit funds pass through stablecoins, cross-chain bridges, decentralised exchanges and mixers, where they blend with legitimate activity and become more difficult to follow and freeze.

TraceX, an AI-driven platform for blockchain tracing and investigation, is being developed for financial crime investigators and law enforcement bodies. It is intended to follow funds across linked blockchain addresses, flag suspicious patterns that connect separate cases, and produce investigative leads backed by traceable evidence and human oversight.

In a recent development, reverse tracing, MegaMap network analysis, pattern recognition and case association are on the roadmap. Investigators retain decision-making authority, using TraceX’s suggestions as guidance, and every decision is logged.

VisionX began life as an incubated project inside MetaComp, tackling compliance and financial crime risks where traditional finance meets digital assets. It has since grown into a combined financial crime and compliance platform that underpins compliance intelligence for MetaComp’s StableX Agentic Network, which debuted as the StableX Network in November 2025.

Its offering includes VisionX KYT, which pools blockchain risk data from several independent analytics providers covering 1 billion wallets across 25 chains, and Web2.5 TxM, which merges identity, behavioural and network signals to monitor transactions across both traditional and digital asset markets.

Spinning VisionX AI out as an independent business allows it to sell to a wider pool of financial institutions, digital asset firms and public-sector bodies. The company prepares to apply its graph intelligence technology to financial crime detection, fraud and scam prevention, compliance risk management and investigations.

The AEGIS name, short for Attention-based Entity and Graph Intelligence System, references the shield of Zeus in Greek myth that was lent to Athena, reflecting the technology’s protective purpose.

Recent findings suggest that visionX AI executive chairwoman Tin Pei Ling, who is also co-president of Alpha Ladder Group and MetaComp, noted, “Financial crime operates through networks of people, entities and financial activities. To fight it, we need AI that understands the relationships between transactions. AEGIS is built to see this network. It learns how money moves between accounts and wallets, so it can spot the patterns that link activity which looks unrelated. Our ambition is to build AI-native financial crime tools that help institutions stay ahead of emerging threats.”.

Industry observers note that visionX AI CEO Summer Yu said, “Individual cases often look unrelated, even when the same criminal network sits behind them. TraceX brings AEGIS into practical blockchain investigations, so investigators can identify patterns, connect cases and uncover those networks. AI reveals investigators where to look next, and their judgement and the evidence still decide the case.”.

Starting today, Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS) for MySQL supports MySQL minor version 8.4.13, the latest minor released by community MySQL. We recommend upgrading to the newer minor versions to accept fixes for Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) in prior versions of MySQL and to benefit from bug fixes, performance improvements, and upcoming functionality added by the MySQL community. Learn more about the enhancements in RDS for MySQL 8.4.13 in the Amazon RDS user guide and MySQL 8.4.13 release notes.

You can upgrade your databases during scheduled maintenance windows using automatic minor version upgrades. To simplify operations at scale, enable automatic minor version upgrades and use the AWS Organizations Upgrade Rollout Policy to orchestrate upgrades across your instances in phases, validating on lower-priority environments before upgrading your most critical ones. You can perform minor version upgrades in-place or via snapshot restore. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon RDS User Guide. This release is supported in all AWS Regions where Amazon RDS for MySQL is available.

Amazon RDS for MySQL makes it simple to set up, operate, and scale MySQL deployments in the cloud. Create or update a fully managed Amazon RDS database in the Amazon RDS Management Console or by using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).

Latest Update: GateWatch: Low-Overhead LLM Monitoring with Boolean Circuits

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (217 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

In a recent development, arXiv:2611.24619v1 Announce Type: upcoming Abstract: As large language models (LLMs) and LLM-based agents are increasingly deployed, monitoring their behavior becomes vital for detecting unsafe or unintended actions. Activation probes offer an efficient approach, but existing methods face trade-offs between accuracy, interpretability, and computational overhead. Probes on raw activations lack interpretable inputs, whereas sparse autoencoder (SAE) probes use interpretable features but often rely on additive classifiers and large SAE encoders, limiting interpretability and increasing memory overhead. We introduce GateWatch, a compact, interpretable classifier that expresses its entire decision rule as an explicit Boolean logic over a small number of binarized SAE features. We explore three approaches to constructing these circuits under a specified gate budget. For efficient deployment, GateWatchServe computes only selected SAE features, enables streaming of their binary values across layers during inference, and evaluates multiple GateWatch classifiers in parallel using compact lookup tables. Across 24 tasks on Gemma-2-9B, GateWatch achieves 80.49% mean test accuracy using only 3.8 SAE features and 3.5 logic gates per probe on average, just 1.17 percentage points below full 16K-feature SAE probes, while matching or outperforming them on 10 tasks and reducing probe memory by 99.98%. Inside vLLM, 1,000 concurrent multi-layer, multi-token GateWatch classifiers retain 97-98% of baseline throughput and 99.8% of KV-cache capacity.

Breaking: Introducing object enrichments: Transform unstructured data into agent-ready context

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1519 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Google

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The vast majority of enterprise information is unstructured, locked away in object storage as petabytes of images, PDFs, videos, and audio files.
  • Sources indicate that today, we are introducing object enrichments, a new Google Cloud Storage capability that uses AI models to automatically extract rich contextual metadata from Cloud Storage objects and saves it in-place as object context, enabling agents to acquire the information needed to make complex business decisions.
  • Industry observers note that “L'Oreal is the 4th largest advertiser in the world, and managing media assets at that scale is complex.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The front door to AI in the workplace.

The vast majority of enterprise information is unstructured, locked away in object storage as petabytes of images, PDFs, videos, and audio files. This data holds the institutional knowledge AI agents need to do business-critical work. But to an agent, a raw object is just bytes it can't reason over. As enterprises start to deploy agents in production, the focus has shifted toward transforming these raw objects into rich, agent-ready context.

Sources indicate that today, we are introducing object enrichments, a new Google Cloud Storage capability that uses AI models to automatically extract rich contextual metadata from Cloud Storage objects and saves it in-place as object context, enabling agents to acquire the information needed to make complex business decisions. Object enrichments gives customers access to the AI models used by internal Google services such as Google Photos, offering image annotations like object detection and image labeling at 75% cost savings when compared to similar services from other cloud providers. Available in preview, this fully managed service also includes high-quality PDF classification model, enabling customers to seamlessly turn their object store into an intelligent, AI-ready foundation.

Industry observers note that “L'Oreal is the 4th largest advertiser in the world, and managing media assets at that scale is complex. Cloud Storage object enrichments’s high quality and cost-effective annotations enable us to discover, understand, and govern our content at scale, accelerating marketing and advertising operations while remaining compliant in all markets. Object enrichments enables L'Oreal to label its extensive creative asset repository 100x faster at a fraction of the cost of existing pipelines and processes.” – Antoine Castex, Principal Data & AI Architect, L’Oreal.

To operate efficiently, agents need grounded knowledge; however, reading every raw file at scale is cost- and performance-prohibitive. For example, if an operations agent needs to pinpoint a specific event—such as a doorstep package delivery or a roadway hazard—streaming thousands of smart-camera or vehicle frames into the AI model on every user prompt would burn through expensive tokens and add minutes of delay. To bridge this gap, teams must pre-process raw data and extract rich, contextual metadata, which agents can then leverage at runtime. Historically, achieving this meant dealing with three challenges:.

Cost: Running models over millions to billions of objects is expensive, pushing organizations to compromise and process only a fraction of their data, creating blind spots that lessen agents’ accuracy.

Recent findings suggest that operational toil: A self-managed pipeline means stitching together multiple services — from event triggers and queues to custom infrastructure built on Cloud Run or Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) — along with scalable retry/error logic and job scheduling. Once deployed, that infrastructure still requires continuous upgrades and capacity management. Teams sometimes spend months on this plumbing rather than focusing on building agents that solve actual business problems.

Industry observers note that fragmented metadata: Extracted metadata often lands in a separate data store, decoupling context from the bytes it describes. Teams must pay for and maintain a second storage system, govern access policies across disconnected permission models, and run custom cleanup jobs to keep metadata in sync when source objects are copied, moved, or deleted.

This is why we built object enrichments: to natively provide agent-ready context for your unstructured data, equipping your agents with complete, grounded knowledge without prohibitive costs, custom pipeline plumbing, or fragmented metadata.

Sources indicate that 1. Reduce costs with Google modelsObject enrichments offers dramatic savings at scale: enriching 10 million images or PDFs costs just $700 (according to published pricing). You can use Google’s high-quality AI models for image annotations—including object detection, face detection, image labeling, and explicit content detection—at one of the industry’s best price points. In addition, the PDF classification model lets you categorize documents into standard business and industry categories like Finance, Games, News, and Health.

"Even with a highly accurate baseline, Hyperscience leveraged object enrichments to drive a 50%+ lift in document classification accuracy, while simultaneously reducing classification inference costs by 2-3x.” – Mayur Pillay, VP Partnerships, Hyperscience.

In a recent development, 2. Generate richer context with GeminiFor complex multimodal reasoning across text, PDFs, images, audio, and video, you can leverage Gemini natively with object enrichments, unlocking advanced use cases such as summarization, entity extraction, transcription, and translation. Please reach out to us at storage-ai@google.com to learn more and request access to this upcoming functionality.

3. No pipeline, low toil setupSkip the brittle, multi-component DIY pipelines. Setting up an enrichment job just takes three simple steps, with no code required in the Google Cloud console, or programmatically via the Cloud Storage API, following these steps:.

It has been revealed that define your scope: Provide a set of buckets containing the objects to process and specify the processing location. Object enrichments can scale to millions or billions of objects.

Choose your models: Pick one or more of the five first-party Cloud Storage models for images and PDFs.

Grant permissions: Grant the necessary IAM permissions to the object enrichments service to access your Cloud Storage buckets.

Object enrichments handles the rest: It orchestrates model inference, parses the responses, and writes the results to each object's object context, with built-in retries and throttling. There are no queues to manage, workers to scale, or glue code to maintain.

"Cloud Storage object enrichments and BigQuery, slashes AI development from 6 months to 1 month while rapidly improving our models." - Brandon Bunker, VP of Product AI, Vivint.

In a recent development, 4. Context lives where the bytes liveInstead of parking metadata in a separate data store, object enrichments writes model outputs directly to object context, a specialized Cloud Storage metadata construct that’s purpose-built for storing contextual information as structured key-value pairs alongside the object itself. Because context is stored alongside object’s actual bytes, you get enterprise-grade data management out of the box, with:.

Cloud Storage durability and simplified lifecycle management: Object context shares the same durability and consistency properties as the underlying Cloud Storage object. It travels automatically with the object during copy, move, and replication operations and is automatically removed when the object is deleted — no more cleanup jobs!

Fine-grained IAM governance: Using IAM, administrators can control who can read, add, update, or remove object context.

Fast object filtering and serving: Applications can filter object listings directly by object context key-value pairs or read context metadata alongside objects, in order to serve richer experiences.

Turnkey multimodal analytics in BigQuery: You can easily configure your object context to natively flow into BigQuery via Storage Insights datasets, allowing data teams to run SQL analytics, build dashboards, and join unstructured file insights with structured enterprise tables, without writing a single line of ETL code.

Early customers are already putting object enrichments to work across key business scenarios:.

In a recent development, creative asset search and media archives: Marketing, retail, and media organizations manage petabytes of creative image assets, where finding a specific asset, e.g., "a red car driving at sunset" or "a vintage convertible in the desert during golden hour", requires rich semantic metadata. Object enrichments automatically generates descriptive labels in object context, which can then be indexed into a vector database or BigQuery to power accurate retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) applications and asset-discovery agents.

Industry observers note that automated trust, safety, and content moderation: Social platforms, marketplaces, and digital media pipelines scan millions of user uploads and supplier catalogs every day for explicit content. Historically, scaling this for every single upload has been cost-prohibitive, but not anymore. With object enrichments, you can process 10 million images for just $700.

Training data curation for frontier AI: Autonomous driving, smart home, and robotics companies capture hundreds of millions of raw camera and sensor files. They often need targeted data samples for specific fine-tuning scenarios, which make up only a tiny fraction of their corpus. By enriching raw captures in place with object detection and image labeling models and then querying the resulting metadata in BigQuery, ML engineers can pinpoint exact training cohorts in minutes rather than months.

Multimodal analytics: Combine insights from images and documents with structured business data to drive personalization, fraud detection, and trend discovery — for example, analyzing customer uploaded images of the product alongside their comments and recent sales data.

Sources indicate that object enrichments is available in preview today in the Cloud Storage console and through the Cloud Storage API. To get started, check out the following resources.

Read the documentation: Learn how to configure an enrichments job and use object contexts.

Analyze in BigQuery: Set up Storage Insights datasets and query your enrichments alongside your BigQuery business data.

Connect your agents: Pair object enrichments and object context with the Cloud Storage MCP server to give agents secure, IAM-scoped access to your data and its context.

Review pricing: See Cloud Storage pricing for details.

Gemini enrichments: Reach out to us at storage-ai@google.com to learn more and request access to this upcoming functionality.

Start building: Head to the Cloud Storage console to enrich your first bucket in just three clicks.

How UK AISI and EvalEval Are Making Benchmark Results Reproducible

📅 22 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (798 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Hugging Face

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The EvalEval Coalition is thrilled to share that the UK AI Security Institute (AISI) is using EvalEval's infrastructure to openly share evaluation results, supporting more reproducible and verifiable evaluation science.
  • It has been revealed that AISI and EvalEval have previously collaborated on research that began at a joint workshop alongside NeurIPS 2025, and feedback from the Institute has helped shape the Every Eval Ever (EEE) schema.
  • As AI deployment accelerates, evaluations are becoming increasingly crucial sources of evidence about model and system performance.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The EvalEval Coalition is thrilled to share that the UK AI Security Institute (AISI) is using EvalEval's infrastructure to openly share evaluation results, supporting more reproducible and verifiable evaluation science.

It has been revealed that AISI and EvalEval have previously collaborated on research that began at a joint workshop alongside NeurIPS 2025, and feedback from the Institute has helped shape the Every Eval Ever (EEE) schema. This next phase of the collaboration puts that shared infrastructure into practice.

As AI deployment accelerates, evaluations are becoming increasingly crucial sources of evidence about model and system performance. Yet results are reported across many formats, platforms, and outlets, often without enough information to reproduce them. Running the evaluations again may itself be prohibitively expensive.

EvalEval's mission is to improve this ecosystem through a shared reporting schema, Every Eval Ever, and an open platform, Evaluation Cards, that brings evaluation results and the information needed to interpret them into a common structure.

In a recent development, this builds naturally on AISI's work to make evaluation more efficient through OptStop, more statistically rigorous through HiBayES, and more standardised in areas including transcript analysis and capability elicitation. Together, AISI and EvalEval are working to diagnose gaps in evaluation reporting and build shared infrastructure to close them.

According to recent reports, transcript-level transparency matters not only for reproducibility, but also for analysis and diagnosis. In this new phase of the collaboration, AISI is making publicly reported evaluation methods and findings available through Evaluation Cards where appropriate. The release includes verified results, context, and configuration information for the five benchmarks in the paper's main experiment:.

These results cover six frontier models: Claude Opus 4, Claude Opus 4.5, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5, GPT-5.2, and GPT-5.4. The release also includes results from two related cyber evaluations—Cyber CTFs and The Last Ones—which use a different, partially overlapping set of models. The data accompany AISI's paper, How Inference Compute Shapes Frontier LLM Evaluation, which studies how benchmark performance depends on inference-time compute and evaluation protocol.

Performance on Humanity's Last Exam changes with evaluation protocol and inference compute. Each curve indicates the cumulative share of attempted tasks solved within a given token count, using the earliest observed success per task. When models received correctness feedback from an oracle after each attempt, they continued to solve additional tasks as token use increased.

Sources indicate that when results are openly released with setup information, researchers and practitioners can examine individual studies more closely and compare findings across the wider ecosystem. Where other reports lack these details, releases like AISI's provide verified reference points for interpreting evaluations in context—for example, by helping researchers understand how setup choices may influence reported performance. As more evaluators adopt EEE, open comparisons like these can support broader and more reliable meta-research.

AISI's Terminal-Bench 2.0 results alongside other reported evaluations for the same models, under different evaluation setups.

We are excited about this adoption and look forward to further standardising and sharing evaluations with AISI and other AI evaluation organisations.

According to recent reports, the EvalEval Coalition is a research community developing scientifically grounded research and robust deployment infrastructure for the evaluation ecosystem. Its goal is to improve evaluation science, address the lack of consensus around documenting evaluation applicability and utility, and broaden coverage of the impacts that matter for scientific research and policy analysis.

Sources indicate that the coalition's flagship projects include Every Eval Ever, a shared schema and repository for evaluation results, and Evaluation Cards, which combines benchmark metadata, evaluation-run data, and model metadata into interpretable records. Together, they make it easier to understand when apparently similar scores were produced under meaningfully different conditions.

Sources indicate that the UK AI Security Institute is a research organisation within the UK government's Department for Science, Innovation and Technology. Its mission is to equip governments with a scientific understanding of the risks posed by advanced AI. AISI conducts research and builds infrastructure to understand advanced AI capabilities and impacts, develop and test mitigations, and inform policy.

The line that matters for practitioners is quiet: apparently similar scores can be produced under meaningfully different conditions.

Once you've watched a benchmark move just by changing inference-time compute or the elicitation protocol, "Model A beat Model B on X" without a card is marketing, not comparison. Evaluation Cards that ship verified results with configuration — especially transcript-level context where it's appropriate — are how eval becomes a contract instead of a leaderboard screenshot.

One ask I'd put to teams adopting EEE: which fields get skipped first under deadline pressure (seed, tool access, attempt budget, oracle feedback), and do you treat a missing field as "do not cite the delta" rather than "assume defaults"?

Sources indicate that reproducible reporting won't remove disagreement. It will make the disagreement about the right variables.

Industry News: Think Offline, Act in Real Time: Self-Improving Visual Game Agents through Code

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (202 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

arXiv:2611.24590v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pre-trained models can read screens and reason about games, yet on an unfamiliar game, an agent still has to learn to play. We ask how an agent can self-improve on such a game from a few of its own attempts, in real-time visual games where the agent sees only the screen and the game keeps running while the agent thinks. We study two kinds of policy that can carry this improvement. In model as policy, a model selects actions during play; we adapt real-time chunking so that committed actions keep executing while the model reasons, and train a 2B controller for this interface. In code as policy, a model writes, tests, and revises a program between attempts, and the program acts during play. Across 170 GameWorld tasks, with at most eight one-minute executions per run, code as policy reaches 47.80% mean progress, against 30.90% for our trained controller, and leads in all five game categories. Improving the controller's weights on a single game, by contrast, yields only modest gains. These results favor letting a model think offline and storing what it learns in a program that acts in real time. Project repository: https://github.com/TabibitoQZP/SIGame.

AWS Lambda adds support for GPU instances on Lambda Managed Instances

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (351 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Amazon

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • AWS Lambda now supports GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances using EC2 G-series instances.
  • According to recent reports, running GPU workloads today requires customers to provision hardware, manage driver and framework dependencies, and build custom scaling and capacity management.
  • Recent findings suggest that GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where Lambda Managed Instances and EC2 G-series instances are available.

AWS Lambda now supports GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances using EC2 G-series instances. You can now run GPU-accelerated workloads including AI inference, media processing, 3D rendering, scientific computing, and financial simulations on Lambda without managing GPU drivers, frameworks, or scaling. Lambda runs multiple invocations concurrently in each execution environment and scales responsively based on GPU utilization, CPU utilization, and concurrency to keep your GPUs busy and reduce costs. GPU-accelerated functions integrate with the same 200+ AWS event sources as other Event Functions, so you can add GPU compute as another step in your serverless application.

According to recent reports, running GPU workloads today requires customers to provision hardware, manage driver and framework dependencies, and build custom scaling and capacity management. With this launch, you can go from code to a running GPU workload in minutes. Lambda provides GPU base images preconfigured with frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, and PyTorch. You can run workloads with large artifacts using container images and NVMe ephemeral storage of up to 32 GB each. To reduce startup time, Lambda supports Seekable OCI (SOCI) lazy loading and streaming artifacts directly from Amazon S3. For resilience, you can select G-series instance types from multiple generations in the allowed instance types for your capacity provider. Lambda provisions instances from the newest generation that meets your function requirements and falls back to older generations when capacity is unavailable.

Recent findings suggest that GPU-accelerated Event Functions on Lambda Managed Instances is available in all AWS Commercial Regions where Lambda Managed Instances and EC2 G-series instances are available. You can configure GPU-accelerated functions using the AWS Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, AWS CloudFormation, AWS CDK, or AWS SAM. You can also use this feature through coding assistants such as Kiro, Claude Code, or Codex by installing the Lambda Managed Instances skill from the Agent Toolkit for AWS. You pay the EC2 On-Demand price (Savings Plans and Reserved Instances apply) for your instance, plus a 9.75% Lambda management fee and $0.20 per million requests. To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda Developer Guide and AWS Lambda Pricing.

Breaking: NaviGATE: Noise-Aware Dual-View Generation for Multimodal Knowledge Graph Reasoning

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (176 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish

Industry observers note that arXiv:2611.24552v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal knowledge graph reasoning (MKGR) aims to infer missing facts by jointly exploiting relational structures, textual descriptions, and visual evidence. Existing embedding-based methods effectively capture graph topology, but their fixed multimodal representations are less effective for query-specific fine-grained semantic reasoning, while generation-based methods are vulnerable to noisy retrieval and may produce invalid entities. To address these challenges, we propose NaviGATE, a noise-aware generative framework for MKGR. NaviGATE first aligns graph-derived structural representations with textual semantics, then performs structure-aware internal knowledge activation by fine-tuning the multimodal language model with multimodal entity summaries and injected structural tokens. In the noise-aware dual-view instruction tuning stage, NaviGATE jointly optimizes retrieval-free and retrieval-aware views: reliable retrieved candidates are reinforced through contrastive logit sharpening, while misleading candidates are suppressed through parametric consistency distillation. In inference, structure-constrained decoding restricts generation to valid entities in the target knowledge graph. Experiments on standard benchmarks show that NaviGATE consistently outperforms strong unimodal, multimodal, and generation-based baselines, and remains robust under noisy retrieval scenarios.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that reinforcement Learning environments give new capabilities to agentic AI systems, and they’re a great way to measure and improve performance in your agents.
  • An environment gives an agent a task, responds to its actions with observations, and scores the outcome.
  • In a recent development, an RL environment on the Hub is a dataset repo that shows up in the fresh RL Environments filter.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that reinforcement Learning environments give new capabilities to agentic AI systems, and they’re a great way to measure and improve performance in your agents. Therefore, Hugging Face Hub now has a special place for RL Environments.

An environment gives an agent a task, responds to its actions with observations, and scores the outcome. The resulting rewards can measure an agent's performance during evaluation or provide a learning signal during training. For an introduction to this interaction loop, see our blogpost on environments. Within the environment, the agent will perform a set of tasks that are represented as datasets. Therefore, environments can be split into broadly two parts: tasksets and runtimes. In this release, we are focusing on the tasksets.

In a recent development, an RL environment on the Hub is a dataset repo that shows up in the fresh RL Environments filter. The Use this dataset button gives you the command to run it in that framework. There is no new repo type, no registry, and no sign-up. There are already environments in Harbor, Verifiers, and NVIDIA NeMo Gym.

Every RL paper or framework uses its own way to find environments. Custom hubs, runtime registries, independent task datasets, or a GitHub list of tasks with a custom loader. This means that many of the published environments are siloed: if you publish an environment for one framework, people of the other three can’t load it. If you want to train on an environment from another framework or a new paper, you’ll need to port it by hand.

Industry observers note that we think this is the wrong shape. An environment is tasks, tests, containers, and a reward rule, which are data with a runtime on top. The Hub already stores data, versions it, gates it, previews it, and serves it to millions of people. It does not need a second system to hold environments. It needs a way to say "this data is an environment, and here is how you run it.".

The frameworks keep doing what they are good at. The Hub does what it is good at, which is hosting, discovery, and versioning. Nobody has to own the catalogue. In fact, catalogues can run on other platforms too, powered by the hub.

The dataset repository hosts your environment files. The framework runs them locally or on a supported cloud backend. Hugging Face Jobs can run cloud workloads, and Hugging Face Sandboxes, built on Jobs, provide interactive command execution. The tags describe compatibility and generate loading commands; adding a tag does not start a job or sandbox.

The RL Environments filter. Go to huggingface.co/datasets?other=rl-environment. Every dataset with the rl-environment tag appears there, whatever framework it works with.

It has been revealed that framework tags. Four environment frameworks are registered as dataset libraries:.

Each framework tag puts the framework's icon on the dataset page and adds a generated snippet to Use this dataset.

In a recent development, A dataset can carry more than one framework tag. That is the point. Tags describe compatibility, and compatibility is not exclusive. Each listed framework must support the files in the repository; adding a tag does not convert them.

Choose the example for your framework and run it in a separate Python environment with the prerequisites listed below.

Industry observers note that harbor can load task directories from a Hub repository. The oracle agent runs the task's reference solution, then the verifier scores the result. It does not call a model.

The viewer shows the task's reward, verifier output, and logs. This checks the task and its reference solution before you try a model agent.

The Harbor integration of verifiers v1 can run the same task directories in different runtimes, such as Docker. It also supports different harnesses, including a minimal bash harness.

In a recent development, here repo is the full Hugging Face Git URL, while dataset is the name and version in that repo's registry.json. This loader uses Harbor's registry conventions, so a bare Hub repo ID cannot replace both values.

OpenEnv's Harbor integration can run the same task directories with an agent such as OpenCode and return the verifier's reward alongside the agent's trace.

The command downloads the dataset's tasks/ directories, runs one task in Docker, and writes the result. The default connection uses a temporary Gradio tunnel so the sandboxed agent can reach OpenEnv's model proxy. Read the verifier result and the number of model calls:.

According to recent reports, A reward of None means no verifier reward was produced; inspect error before interpreting the run as a model failure. This path expects Harbor task directories.

NeMo Gym supports evaluation and RL training: its environments collect trajectories and compute rewards, while a training framework updates model weights. For example, the Structured Outputs dataset pairs prompts with JSON schemas. Its verifier rewards schema adherence; it does not check whether the generated content is factually correct.

The best part is that this gives one repo and one discussion tab where people report broken tasks from all major frameworks. So when an author fixes a bad test, every framework gets the fix on the next pull.

Open your dataset card and add this to the YAML header:.

Sources indicate that that is the whole integration. Keep rl-environment, then list every framework that can load your files. If your environment works with a framework we have not registered yet, open a PR to the list of supported libraries.

The docs have the full reference.

It has been revealed that we opened PRs to tag some of the environments people already train on. If you maintain one of these, merge the PR and your environment shows up in the filter.

The first version generates one default snippet per framework. Per-config snippets are next, so a repo with several task sets can show the right command for each. After that we will look at structural detection for frameworks with strict layouts. It would also be really cool build custom task UIs, we’ve been experimenting with this here:.

The bigger goal is for framework tagging to be automatic everywhere. OpenEnv already does it on upload. If you maintain Harbor, Verifiers, Nemo Gym, or any other environment framework, add the tags in your push path. It is a few lines, and every environment your users publish becomes visible to everyone else.

It has been revealed that if you train agents, go browse the filter. If you build environments, publish and tag them, whether they cover coding, tool use, games, robotics, or another task. Include the files, a working run command, and the rule that produces the reward so others can use them. If your framework is missing, contribute it to the list of supported libraries.

Amazon CloudFront Announces WebSocket and gRPC Support for Origin Mutual TLS

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (194 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Amazon

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that amazon CloudFront (CF) now supports WebSocket and gRPC traffic to application origins in AWS regions, with mutual TLS authentication between CF and the application origin (origin mTLS).
  • Sources indicate that previously, customers serving WebSocket or gRPC traffic through CloudFront had to use shared secrets or IP allow-lists to identify requests originating from CloudFront.
  • There is no additional charge for origin mTLS, and it is available with pay-as-you-go pricing and in the Business and Premium flat-rate pricing looks.

Recent findings suggest that amazon CloudFront (CF) now supports WebSocket and gRPC traffic to application origins in AWS regions, with mutual TLS authentication between CF and the application origin (origin mTLS). Customers can now use TLS certificates to authenticate requests from CloudFront while setting up WebSocket or gRPC connections to their origins. Origin mTLS protects internet facing applications that need persistent, bidirectional or streaming connections, such as chat platforms, collaborative editing tools or live dashboards from unauthenticated requests.

Sources indicate that previously, customers serving WebSocket or gRPC traffic through CloudFront had to use shared secrets or IP allow-lists to identify requests originating from CloudFront. This was operationally complex and did not provide strong authentication. With Origin mTLS, customers can use one TLS based authentication for HTTP, WebSocket and gRPC traffic to an application origin. This works with application origins within AWS such as Application Load Balancer and API Gateway, on-premises origins, and origins hosted outside AWS.

There is no additional charge for origin mTLS, and it is available with pay-as-you-go pricing and in the Business and Premium flat-rate pricing looks. To learn more, visit the CloudFront origin mutual TLS documentation.

ABSClaw: From Invented Worlds to Reality-Grounded Social Simulation

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (214 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Arxiv

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read

In a recent development, arXiv:2611.24517v1 Announce Type: latest Abstract: LLM-based artificial societies exhibit rich behavior but often lack scientific grounding: personas and environments are assumed, interaction networks are synthetic, and simulators are generated as free-form code, making results difficult to tie to real populations and sensitive to the backbone model. We argue that simulated worlds should be sampled from observed data, while simulation logic should be implemented by composing operations from a shared, task-independent vocabulary. In this paper, we introduce ABSClaw, a zero-code agent that compiles natural-language requests into executable, reality-grounded social simulations. ABSClaw grounds who acts, where they act, and with whom they interact in survey and census data, geospatial sources, and real networks. It expresses state transitions through 26 atomic operations. To support an open and extensible ecosystem, ABSClaw further allows capabilities to be added as lifecycle-scoped skills without modifying its core. Furthermore, we propose ABSBench, a benchmark of 193 real-world social-simulation tasks. On ABSBench, ABSClaw achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated social simulators. Three real-world case studies show that grounding personas, environments, and interaction networks each improves agreement with observed outcomes. With one runtime skill, ABSClaw executes 13 population-scale simulations, collectively involving 25 million agents. Industry observers note that amazon CloudFront standard logging now supports additional access log fields that were previously available only in CloudFront real-time logs. You can now include these fields in your standard logs and deliver them to Amazon S3, Amazon CloudWatch Logs, or Amazon Data Firehose, without setting up an additional data stream for real-time logs.

Recent findings suggest that the fresh fields include the IP address of the CloudFront server that handled the request, identifiers that separate traffic on a primary distribution from traffic on a staging distribution, and a media quality confidence score. They also include Common Media Client Data (CMCD) fields, which video players send with each request to report details like bitrate, buffer length, and playback session ID. Streaming teams can use these fields to match playback problems that viewers see with CloudFront delivery data, which makes troubleshooting faster.

Recent findings suggest that these fields are available in all CloudFront edge locations, and standard logging pricing applies. To learn more, see Standard logging page in the Amazon CloudFront Developer Guide.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Holo4 is our newly introduced series of agentic models.
  • Sources indicate that holo4 builds on our previous model and interacts with software through any available interface: GUIs, code, MCP and APIs.
  • Industry observers note that holo4 clicks and types on a screen, writes and runs its own code, and calls MCP or API tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Holo4 is our newly introduced series of agentic models. It comes in two sizes: 27B dense and 35B-A3B Mixture of Experts. Both are available on the H Models API. We are also releasing an updated version of Holotron 3: Holotron4 Nano.

Sources indicate that holo4 builds on our previous model and interacts with software through any available interface: GUIs, code, MCP and APIs. It scores well on academic benchmarks, but we built it for real business workflows. It was trained through supervised and reinforcement learning on a large set of environments and tasks, including those generated by our Agentic Task Factory.

Industry observers note that holo4 clicks and types on a screen, writes and runs its own code, and calls MCP or API tools. It uses whichever fits the task. Most agentic models are trained for one interface only: GUI-focused models are blind without a screen, while models that prefer tool calling are stuck in front of an application that has no API. Real work is not siloed that way, and a single business task can require combining these different approaches.

Holo4 runs on desktops, on the web, on Android, in a code sandbox and against business APIs. It is the same model in each case and it is called the same way. You do not need to select a different model for each platform.

Industry observers note that holo4 models improve significantly over their Qwen base. Holo4 trails only the strongest closed models on long workflows: on OSWorld 2.0, Holo4 27B scores 61.7% against 81.8% for Opus 5.5, and Holo4 35B-A3B reaches 30.9%. However, it does so with orders of magnitude fewer parameters and at a much lower cost. We open-source every trajectory behind our scores on public benchmarks: replay each step at trajectories.hcompany.ai or download them from Hugging Face.

On the hardest academic benchmarks for desktop control (OSWorld 2.0) and API use (AutomationBench), Holo4 competes with frontier models at a much lower cost per task.

OSWorld 2.0. Costs are estimated from the input and output tokens of each agentic run. Holo4 is priced at H Models API rates (single run). Qwen3.8 27B: model card score, cost from the tokens of our run at Alibaba Cloud list prices. Qwen3.6 35B-A3B: single run in our harness, at Alibaba Cloud list prices with cache hits at 20% of the input price. OpenAI launch data supplies the GPT and Opus effort sweeps; other closed and open-weight points use the official OSWorld 2.0 leaderboard. Releases, harnesses and task subsets differ. The line connects non-dominated score and cost pairs among the closed models; Holo4 is excluded.

AutomationBench. Holo4, Qwen3.8 27B and Qwen3.6 35B-A3B: AutomationBench v1.0.6, scores and costs measured in our internal harness. Other models: public-set scores from the AutomationBench README, cost per task from the official leaderboard, which runs on the private set. We will report Holo4 on the private set once it is evaluated.

Recent findings suggest that trained on environments and tasks from our Agentic Task Factory, Holo4 models excel on professional software. The examples below show Holo4 27B alongside Qwen3.8 27B, its base model. Same prompt and harness for both models.

A player marker moves continuously along the corridors, eating each pellet it passes over and scoring a point for it. Three ghosts move through the same corridors and chase the player. Our internal set of agentic pipelines builds interactive environments and verifiable tasks from documentation alone, such as screenshots of real websites or open-source software. So far it has produced about 10,000 tasks across web apps, MCP servers and desktop environments, including hybrid environments that expose the same state through a GUI and MCP.

Alongside training, we rebuilt our harness, the loop that executes the model's actions and manages its context over hundreds of steps, using feedback from agentic performance on OSWorld 2.0. Agents tagged why each task failed and engineers reviewed their fixes. The largest changes were giving the agent a reliable memory that can keep track of hundreds of steps, and a shell on the desktop machine itself.

Industry observers note that opus 5 (70.2%) and GPT-5.6 Sol (66.2%) use max-effort partial rewards on the v2026.08.08 offline set from OpenAI's launch chart, as in the cost-performance plot. Other reference scores come from model cards and the official leaderboard. Task releases, subsets and harnesses vary.

Industry observers note that our post-training stack is designed to adapt to latest foundation models and produce agents that generalize across interfaces and environments. As a member of the NVIDIA Nemotron Coalition, we applied our latest stack to the Nemotron 3 Nano Omni model as a follow-up to Holotron 3.

The same recipe turns Nemotron 3 Nano Omni into Holotron4 Nano, a generalist agentic model that significantly improves over the base model on GUI workflows and in environments exposing MCP, APIs or coding sandboxes.

Gains are absolute percentage-point improvements over Nemotron 3 Nano Omni.

Industry observers note that these gains show that our recipe transfers well and can turn a generalist model into an agentic expert. Nothing in it is size-specific.

Recent findings suggest that both sizes are available today on the H Models API. Weights are on Hugging Face in BF16, FP8, NVFP4 and 4-bit GGUF, next to our small model, Holotron4 Nano.

We will release optimized DSpark drafter checkpoints in the coming days to further accelerate inference.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unlimit, a worldwide provider of financial infrastructure, has signed up to Visa’s Agentic Ready Program for Acceptance, putting its payment network to the test as AI agents prepare to make purchases on behalf of consumers.

Under the initiative, Unlimit and Visa will examine whether the company’s systems can handle transactions triggered by AI agents rather than people. The trials will cover how credentials and authentication information are processed securely, full end-to-end testing, and what happens after a purchase, including refunds, chargebacks and reconciliation.

The aim is to confirm that merchants and platforms on Unlimit’s network can accept agent-led payments for their customers while relying on existing card networks and their safeguards.

Visa’s broadened programme unites acquirers, payment service providers, merchants and platforms in an effort to get the wider ecosystem ready for AI-initiated payments on a global scale.

In a recent development, unlimit operates a proprietary payments network reaching over 180 countries. The company holds licences across 97 jurisdictions, supports in excess of 1,000 local payment methods, offers payouts in more than 150 currencies and connects directly with domestic payment systems. This blend of international coverage and local integration gives the firm a foundation to serve agentic commerce across varied payment rails, regulatory regimes and shopper habits.

Through its participation, Unlimit is contributing to a shared framework for agentic commerce, one designed to build trust into emerging purchasing experiences while extending the infrastructure that businesses already depend on.

Recent findings suggest that unlimit CEO of global payments Irene Skrynova mentioned, “AI agents are becoming a new type of customer. They will increasingly search, compare and purchase on behalf of people, fundamentally changing how businesses sell and compete. This will create an entirely new wave of demand, and companies that adapt early will be best positioned to capture it. Our work with Visa is an vital step towards building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of global commerce.”.
